reason: I want to start the fuel reaction, so I'll put one of its named inputs at the reactor.
expectation: Hydrogen will be staged at the reactor, ready to combine with carbon dioxide; I don't expect fuel yet.

alternatives.reason: Carbon dioxide is the other necessary input and could plausibly be staged first.

effect: Hydrogen is staged as expected, and the reactor combination is now available.
reaction: The placement feels like a practical setup step, though it is not exciting on its own.
reason: The two gases are named as the fuel reaction inputs, so I want to run them through the reactor.
expectation: The reactor will produce methane, perhaps along with water for recovery.

alternatives.reason: I considered connecting the water return first, but want to start fuel production now.

effect: The gases made a wet methane stream and revealed a goal to return the reaction water.
reaction: It's satisfying to see the hydrogen loop back into water, alongside the fuel.
reason: The hose at the cooled return port is the only gameplay option and matches the new goal.
expectation: The hose will connect the condensed water back toward treatment.

effect: The return feeds treatment and electrolysis, completing the loop and the chapter.
reaction: I like the concrete payoff that each batch needs less new water.

mostWorthwhile.text: Running the reactor and then connecting the return made the fuel and water cycle understandable as a practical system, with an ongoing payoff.

leastWorthwhile.text: Staging hydrogen felt like a small administrative step; it did not reveal much on its own.

surprise.text: Seeing some hydrogen become water again alongside methane made the recycling connection more vivid.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the input placement was required by the interface and the hose had an explicit destination.

continue.text: Yes, cautiously: the practical fuel and water loop makes me curious what the expedition does next, though this short chapter offered little decision difficulty.
